title: One Gaithersburg biotech's latest marketing push: Selling doomsday kits on Amazon
summary: Emergent BioSolutions, a Gaithersburg biotech company, is expanding into the consumer market by selling its reactive skin decontamination lotion, typically used by governments and the military, on Amazon. This marks one of the company's first forays beyond its usual focus on protecting against bioterrorism threats. The product helps protect against chemical warfare agents like sarin.

title: Kohl's and Aldi are going to be neighbors
summary: Kohl's is shrinking the size of some of its stores and will lease the newly available space to Aldi, the German discount grocery chain. This pilot program will include 5 to 10 locations, allowing Kohl's to cut costs and potentially gain new customers from Aldi shoppers. The announcement came as Kohl's reported a 6.3% sales increase in the last quarter, joining other retailers in positive holiday season performance.

title: Amdocs Announces a Strategic Collaboration with Amazon Web Services
summary: Amdocs announced a strategic collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) at Mobile World Congress to help Communications Service Providers (CSPs) transition to the cloud for innovation and operational efficiencies. This partnership will focus on migrating Amdocs' Business Support Systems and third-party legacy environments to an optimized hybrid cloud, enabling CSPs to deploy Amdocs products on AWS, and modernizing operations through Amdocs Managed Services Provider practice. The collaboration builds on their existing relationship, aiming to accelerate CSPs' cloud journeys and deliver enhanced digital services.

title: Next Up for Amazon: Checking Accounts
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly in early-stage discussions with major banks, including JPMorgan Chase & Co., to develop a checking-account-like product for its customers. This initiative aims to attract younger customers and those without traditional bank accounts, potentially reducing Amazon's fees to financial firms and providing valuable customer data. The move signifies Amazon's further expansion into its customers' daily lives and raises questions for traditional banks about its competitive impact.

title: Buffett, Bezos, Grainger and Fastenal – What’s Ahead?
summary: This article discusses speculation about Berkshire Hathaway acquiring industrial distributors like Fastenal and Grainger, given Warren Buffett's large cash reserves and his criteria for acquisitions. It examines how Buffett's current distribution strategy through Berkshire eSupply differs from a direct acquisition of major distributors that compete with Amazon Business. The author suggests Buffett is strategically supporting distributors through services rather than engaging in direct competition with e-commerce giants.

title: Home Shopping Networks QVC and HSN Get a Corporate Rebranding
summary: Liberty Interactive Corp., parent company of QVC and HSN, is rebranding as Qurate Retail Group. This new entity will include QVC, HSN, Zulilly, and several home furnishing brands, aiming to provide curated collections to a global customer base. The rebrand marks a strategic shift to combine retail, media, and social elements while preserving each brand's distinct identity.

title: Podell of Cushman & Wakefield leads panel on NY retail at the WX February breakfast
summary: A panel led by Joanne Podell of Cushman & Wakefield at the WX New York Women Executives in Real Estate breakfast discussed the state of New York retail. Key topics included the competition between brick-and-mortar stores and e-commerce, the slowdown in leasing, and the expected continued retail growth in 2018 driven by holiday sales and technology advancements. Panelists noted the need for traditional stores to innovate and for online retailers to consider physical locations.

title: Leggett & Platt site now leveled for Fuqua’s mixed-use Madison Yards
summary: The former Leggett & Platt manufacturing site in Reynoldstown has been leveled for Jeff Fuqua's $250 million Madison Yards mixed-use development. This project along Memorial Drive and the planned Beltline corridor will include 550 residences, 80,000 sq ft of office space, 160,000 sq ft of retail anchored by a Publix and AMC Theatre, and extensive parking. Construction is expected to begin soon, with a partial delivery anticipated next spring.

title: Birkenstock Seller Files for Bankruptcy, Blames UGGs
summary: Walking Co., a retailer specializing in comfort shoes including Birkenstocks, has filed for its second bankruptcy in less than a decade. The company attributes its financial struggles primarily to the loss of its contract to sell UGG sheepskin boots. This situation highlights the growing challenges retailers face from both online competitors and the very brands they sell.

title: Amazon Prime exec Greg Greeley leaves to run Airbnb’s Homes unit
summary: Greg Greeley, a long-serving and senior executive at Amazon.com Inc., is departing the company to lead Airbnb Inc.'s core home-rental business. Greeley previously oversaw Amazon's Prime membership unit since 2013 and helped develop the program. He was also slated to work on integrating Whole Foods into Amazon's operations.

title: Equinix Power Outage One Reason Behind AWS Cloud Disruption
summary: A power outage at an Equinix data center in Ashburn, Virginia, is at least partially responsible for connectivity issues experienced by some of Amazon's cloud customers. The disruption affected AWS Direct Connect services and was caused by a nor'easter, impacting major AWS customers like Atlassian, Twilio, and Capital One. CoreSite, another data center provider mentioned in the AWS report, stated its facilities did not experience a power outage.

title: Business | Handy Named Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Washington Trust
summary: Edward Handy has been named Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Washington Trust, succeeding Joseph MarcAurele who retired. Mark Gim has taken on the role of President and Chief Operating Officer. The article also reviews the 17 biggest business stories from Rhode Island in 2017, covering topics from company expansions and closures to major financial deals and economic rankings.

title: 5 states with the most "zombie debt" complaints
summary: This article identifies the top five states with the most complaints about "zombie debt," which are old, often uncollectible debts that debt buyers attempt to collect using aggressive tactics. It highlights specific companies frequently involved in these practices and offers advice to consumers on how to dispute such debts. The analysis is based on a study by RewardExpert using Consumer Financial Protection Bureau data.

title: Cigna to Buy Express Scripts in $52 Billion Health Care Deal (Published 2018)
summary: Cigna announced its intention to acquire Express Scripts for $52 billion, a move that reflects the ongoing consolidation within the healthcare industry. The companies claim the merger will benefit consumers by integrating medical and pharmacy histories to improve treatment and reduce costs. This acquisition would also signify the end of Express Scripts as the last major independent pharmacy benefit manager.

title: Local Kroger workers approve new contract
summary: Kroger Co. employees in Cincinnati and Dayton approved a new contract with the UFCW Local 75, raising the starting wage to $10-$11 per hour. The company plans to spend a third of its $400 million annual tax savings on employee investments, including higher starting wages and an education offering, while another third will go to business growth and the remainder to shareholders. This new agreement is seen as a potential model for future contract negotiations in other markets.

title: Midland States promotes 3 top executives
summary: Midland States Bancorp has announced the promotion of three executives as part of a succession plan. The promotions were disclosed on Thursday, March 8, 2018.

title: The retail resurgence this year is deceptive, warns market watcher
summary: A market watcher warns that the apparent retail resurgence in the S&P 500 this year is deceptive, primarily driven by "new retail" companies like Netflix, Amazon, and TripAdvisor rather than traditional brick-and-mortar stores. While many legacy retailers are struggling, some analysts suggest opportunities exist in homebuilding and home improvement retail due to potential financial regulatory rollbacks.

title: Bye-bye, solo Express Scripts: What does the Cigna buyout mean for pharma?
summary: Cigna has acquired Express Scripts in a $54 billion deal, marking another major consolidation in the healthcare industry. This merger, following CVS Health's acquisition of Aetna, is expected to increase pricing pressure on drugmakers. Industry experts believe such consolidation aims to address drug pricing frustrations and enhance negotiating power for insurers.

title: The best sector of this bull market is the ‘greatest investment story ever told’
summary: This article highlights that internet stocks have been the best performing sector during the current nine-year bull market, which began after the financial crisis bottom. It notes that while internet investing is often associated with the dot-com era, the current extended bull market has also seen the sector significantly influence nearly every aspect of the economy. The piece was published on the ninth anniversary of the financial crisis bottom.

title: The best sector of this bull market is the ‘greatest investment story ever told’
summary: This article discusses the internet sector as the best-performing sector in the current bull market, which marks its ninth anniversary since the financial crisis bottom. It highlights how internet stocks have significantly outperformed during this period, influencing nearly every aspect of the economy.

title: The billionaires club: Meet the 10 richest Indian Americans
summary: This article profiles the 10 richest Indian Americans from the 2018 Forbes list of world billionaires. It highlights their origins, educational backgrounds, career paths, net worth, and significant achievements. The list includes notable founders and CEOs across various industries, with two new faces joining the ranks in 2018.

title: John Deere Bets the Farm on AI, IoT
summary: John Deere is significantly investing in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and IoT to modernize its agricultural and heavy equipment. Through acquisitions like Blue River Technology, Deere is developing innovative solutions such as "See and Spray" technology to reduce herbicide use and improve farming efficiency. The company plans to integrate AI and machine learning into all its equipment, utilizing cloud infrastructure and anticipating future advancements with 5G technology.

title: Not just knock-offs, but ‘knockouts’: Inside Kroger’s private label push
summary: Kroger is significantly investing in its private label brands, aiming for "knockout" products that differentiate it from competitors and offer unique items rather than just brand equivalents. The strategy, led by Gil Phipps, senior vice president of Our Brands, leverages Kroger's operational advantages, data science, and culinary innovation to drive sales and compete against aggressive rivals like Walmart, Amazon, Aldi, and Lidl. The success of its Simple Truth organic brand, which reached $2 billion in annual sales, highlights the potential of this focus.

title: Morning Brief: Elliott Reaches Settlement With Akamai
summary: Elliott Management and Akamai Technologies reached a settlement where Akamai agreed to add two independent directors and form a financial operating committee to boost margins. Akamai also increased its share repurchase authorization by $417 million to $750 million. Separately, Steel Partners increased its stake in Babcock & Wilcox, and Saba Capital announced plans to nominate directors to a closed-end mutual fund.

title: Amazon: Prime Video Lured Millions to Shopping Club
summary: Internal Amazon documents reveal that its Prime Video content, specifically its original television shows, attracted over 5 million new subscribers to its Prime shopping club by early 2017. These documents show how Amazon uses video to convert viewers into shoppers, with some shows proving very cost-effective in acquiring new Prime members. The company is now shifting towards more commercially appealing content, including a prequel to "The Lord of the Rings," to further grow its subscriber base, particularly outside the U.S.

title: Toys ‘R’ Us store closures will hurt toy makers like Hasbro and Mattel
summary: The liquidation of Toys "R" Us will significantly impact toy manufacturers like Mattel Inc. and Hasbro Inc., as they lose a major dedicated retailer. These companies relied on Toys "R" Us, which acted as a physical showroom and a crucial check on Amazon.com Inc.'s market dominance. Toy companies will now need to find alternative channels to sell their products.

title: FedEx Announces Billion-Dollar Expansion at Memphis Headquarters
summary: FedEx Corp. is investing over $1 billion to modernize its Memphis, Tenn.-based headquarters, with construction set to begin next year and completion expected by 2025. This expansion, entirely funded by FedEx, includes a new sort facility, state-of-the-art sorting systems, a bulk truckload building, and improved handling for oversize shipments. The project aims to benefit current and future employees and reinforce FedEx's commitment to Tennessee, where it is the largest employer.

title: This May Help Flipkart Demand $20-Billion Valuation From Walmart
summary: Recent markups by several of Flipkart's investors, including Morgan Stanley, Valic Company, Vanguard, and Optimum Fund, have valued the e-commerce giant between $11 billion and $19 billion. This surge in valuation comes as Flipkart negotiates a deal with Walmart, with the Indian retailer aiming for a $20 billion valuation. The strategic investment from Walmart is seen as crucial for Flipkart to compete against rivals like Amazon and Alibaba-funded Paytm in India's fast-growing online retail market.

title: Cognizant, US' Top H-1B Visa Sponsor, Tries to Bury 'Anti-White' Lawsuit
summary: Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp., the leading U.S. sponsor of H-1B visas, is facing a civil rights lawsuit alleging bias against non-Indian workers. Three former employees claim they were replaced by "less qualified" Indians and subjected to discriminatory treatment. Cognizant argues the lawsuit's claims pertain to national origin, not race, and are not covered by federal civil rights law.

title: FedEx Office to Open in 500 Walmart Stores Across US in Next Two Years
summary: FedEx announced it will open 500 FedEx Office locations within Walmart stores nationwide over the next two years, building on a successful pilot program. These new locations will offer packing, shipping, and package receiving services, allowing customers to have packages held for up to five business days. This expansion aims to bring FedEx services closer to consumers and comes amidst Amazon's plans to test its own delivery service.

title: 2016 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos's 2016 Letter to Shareholders discusses the importance of maintaining a "Day 1" mentality to avoid stasis and decline in a large organization. He identifies customer obsession, skepticism of proxies, embracing external trends like AI, and high-velocity decision-making as key elements for Day 1 defense. Bezos emphasizes that customers are always dissatisfied and drive invention, warns against letting processes become proxies for results, and highlights the need to quickly adopt powerful external trends.

title: Here are the 3 groups looking to build an entertainment venue at the Banks: SLIDESHOW (Video)
summary: Three groups have submitted proposals to develop an entertainment venue and event center at The Banks in downtown Cincinnati. This article features a slideshow of renderings, including one from the Live Nation/Ark Group team. The development plans are moving forward with county commissioners.

title: You can now buy Unicorn Magic ice cream
summary: Target has launched a new "Unicorn Magic" ice cream as part of its Market Pantry line. This cherry-flavored ice cream with sour blue raspberry and frosting swirls, and glitter candy bits, is part of a growing trend of unicorn-themed food products from various companies. Other new flavors include Caramel Brownie Moose Tracks, Cherry Chocolate Cake, and Chocolate Coconut.

title: The Importance of NetApp’s Data Fabric Solution
summary: NetApp's Data Fabric solution, launched in 2014 and based on its ONTAP operating system, helps companies simplify data management across various cloud environments, Edge, and data centers. This solution aids in accelerating digital transformation and modernizing storage by leveraging hybrid cloud power. The move to Data Fabric has expanded NetApp's business opportunities and driven revenue growth, with ONTAP software now available on hyperscale clouds like AWS and Microsoft Azure.

title: Starbucks' mobile order push meets resistance from ritual seekers
summary: Starbucks' effort to promote its mobile ordering app is facing unexpected resistance from some customers who value the in-store ritual and interaction with baristas. While the app offers convenience, some customers find it disrupts their routine or can lead to overspending, posing a challenge for Starbucks as it balances tech-savvy demands with its established retail experience. The article also notes how mobile ordering has created new issues, such as customers feeling guilt when skipping lines and baristas struggling with order bottlenecks.

title: Pottery Barn Kids bringing wholesale business to the UK
summary: Williams-Sonoma is expanding its international wholesale operations for Pottery Barn Kids into the UK, including shop-in-shops at John Lewis and a dedicated e-commerce website. This move follows a successful West Elm partnership with John Lewis and is part of Williams-Sonoma's aggressive global expansion strategy for 2018, targeting multi-channel growth in large international markets. The company plans to open 20 new stores globally while closing 30 underperforming ones this year.

title: Exclusive: As Grocery Wars Rage, Target And Kroger Mull A Merger
summary: Target and Kroger are reportedly discussing a potential merger as both companies grapple with Amazon's growing dominance in the grocery market following its acquisition of Whole Foods. The talks, which began last summer, aim to leverage Target's e-commerce strength and Kroger's grocery expertise to compete more effectively, with analysts suggesting such a tie-up would provide crucial infrastructure and market expansion for both retailers.

title: Retail giants Kroger and Target are in merger talks, report claims
summary: Kroger and Target are reportedly in merger talks to potentially combine their businesses, aiming to boost Target's grocery segment and Kroger's e-commerce. If materialized, the merger would create a retail giant with $195 billion in sales across 4,600 stores. However, despite the potential scale, Wells Fargo analyst Edward Kelly expressed concerns about operational distraction and the deal not solving underlying weaknesses for either company.

title: Report: Kroger, Target flirt with mega-merger
summary: Kroger and Target are reportedly discussing a possible mega-merger, with talks ongoing since last summer. The potential deal, valued at over $35 billion, would create a $195 billion sales entity with 4,600 stores nationwide, aiming to better compete against Walmart and Amazon. While Wall Street's reaction was muted, some analysts express skepticism that such a combination would resolve underlying e-commerce weaknesses for either company.

title: The RealReal hires execs from Amazon and Walmart
summary: The RealReal appointed Jun-Sheng Li as chief operating officer and Len Eschweiler as chief revenue officer, both bringing extensive experience from Amazon and Walmart respectively. These hires aim to scale the company's e-commerce operations and sales organization to capitalize on the booming "re-commerce" sector. The luxury resale market, where The RealReal operates, is growing significantly faster than the broader retail market, attracting substantial investor interest and prompting the company's expansion into brick-and-mortar locations.

title: Target, Kroger shares rise on merger report, but source tells CNBC there are no talks
summary: Shares of Target and Kroger experienced a surge in premarket trading following a Fast Company report about potential merger discussions. However, sources close to the matter informed CNBC that no merger talks are occurring; instead, the companies have met regarding a Shipt partnership. Despite the denial, the initial report caused significant stock price movements, highlighting market interest in potential collaborations in the competitive retail and grocery sectors.

title: After crediting tax cuts for new investment, FedEx cancels plan for Greenwood hub
summary: FedEx has canceled its plans to build a $259 million, 608,000-square-foot distribution center in Greenwood, Indiana, two months after crediting Republican tax cuts for new investment. The company cited "projected operational needs" but did not elaborate on its reasons, despite previously stating the hub would create 455 jobs. The city of Greenwood expressed disappointment but noted other companies have shown interest in the location.

title: Walmart and Target stand to gain most from Toys ‘R’ Us liquidation
summary: Walmart and Target are expected to gain the most from the Toys 'R' Us liquidation, capturing a significant portion of the $7 billion in sales up for grabs. A Coresight Research analysis found that a high percentage of Toys 'R' Us shoppers also browsed for toys at Walmart and Target. Amazon's gains are anticipated to be linked to Prime member activity.

title: 10 Personalized Baby Gifts Every New Parent Will Love
summary: This article lists 10 personalized baby gift ideas that new parents will cherish. The suggestions include items like monogrammed hats, custom spoons, personalized blankets, books, and keepsakes that feature the baby's name or birth information. The gifts aim to be unique and memorable for years to come.

title: Why Trump Reportedly Is Taking Aim at Amazon
summary: President Donald Trump is reportedly focused on Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN), believing the e-commerce giant benefits from unfair tax policies and special treatment from the U.S. Postal Service. Sources suggest Trump has even considered antitrust actions against Amazon, fueled by complaints from his real estate friends about the company's impact on brick-and-mortar retail. A significant underlying factor for Trump's animosity may be Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos's ownership of The Washington Post, a newspaper critical of the president.

title: Amazon shares fall after report Trump wants to curb its power
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares dropped by almost 5 percent, wiping over $30 billion off its market value, following a report that U.S. President Donald Trump is concerned about the company's power and wants to use antitrust law against it. Trump also reportedly seeks to change Amazon's tax treatment, an issue he has previously raised publicly. The White House confirmed the President's interest in creating a "level playing field" for businesses but stated no specific policies were on the table.

title: Walmart in early talks to buy health insurer Humana, report says
summary: Walmart is reportedly in preliminary negotiations to acquire Louisville-based health insurer Humana. This potential acquisition would mark Walmart's biggest deal and a significant move into the healthcare sector, aligning with increasing retailer involvement in health services and competition with companies like Amazon. The deal would also expand on Walmart and Humana's existing collaboration on low-cost prescription plans for Medicare customers.

title: |How this 32-year-old high school dropout built a business that sold to Target for $550 million
summary: |Bill Smith, a high school dropout and serial entrepreneur, founded Shipt, an online same-day grocery delivery service, after identifying a need for convenient grocery shopping. Despite an initial failed model, Smith pivoted to grocery delivery after a personal experience and successfully built Shipt by focusing on customer demand and expanding into underserved markets. Shipt was eventually acquired by Target for $550 million, a deal that allowed Target to rapidly expand its same-day delivery services while Shipt continued to operate independently.

title: Opinion: If the FAANGs have got you down, it’s time to win with the WNSSS stocks
summary: This article suggests that investors look beyond the traditional FAANG stocks (Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, Google, Apple) and consider a new set of companies, dubbed "WNSSS" stocks. These include Weibo, Nvidia, ServiceNow, Square, and Shopify, which are posited as potential future market leaders. The piece highlights that while FAANGs have dominated in the past, new tech players are emerging that could offer greater growth opportunities.
